free_to_spend.gloss: What you can still use: your budget minus what's already gone and what's set aside.

protected_reserve.gloss: A slice the app keeps aside and doesn't count as available, so you don't blow the limit by accident.

plan_reserve.gloss: Money your plan already set aside for expected future spending — that's why it isn't in today's free amount.

help_center.title: Help center
help_center.intro: Get answers about the app. Search by a word or browse by topic — it's all local, no AI used.
help_center.no_results: Nothing found for your search. Try another word or browse the topics below.

log_ai.q: How do I log an expense with AI (voice or text)?
log_ai.a: Say or type it in plain language, e.g. "35 on lunch with card" — the AI fills in amount, category and wallet for you to confirm.
steps: Tap the ✨ add button on the home screen
Speak or type the expense, e.g. "20 on a taxi"
Check what the AI understood and save

log_manual.q: How do I log an expense by hand, without AI?
log_manual.a: You can fill everything in manually: amount, category, wallet, date and note — no AI involved.
steps: Open add expense and pick the manual mode
Fill in amount, category and wallet
Adjust date/note if you want and save

log_photo.q: Can I log an expense from a photo of the receipt?
log_photo.a: Yes. Photograph the receipt or pick it from the gallery and the AI reads the amount and suggests the category for you to confirm.
steps: In add expense, tap the camera icon
Take a photo of the receipt or pick from the gallery
Check the read values and save

expenses.q: Where do I see, edit or delete my expenses?
expenses.a: The expenses list holds your full history, with search and filters; tap any item to edit or delete it.
steps: Open the expenses list
Use search and filters to find the entry
Tap it to edit or delete

checkin.q: What is the daily check-in and the honest friend?
checkin.a: A quick read of how your day looks: how much you can use today plus a straight message (the "honest friend"), with no guilt.
steps: On the home screen, open the daily check-in
See today's free amount and the message
Adjust the pace if you want to spend differently

outing.q: How do I use the live outing/night-out mode?
outing.a: Start an outing and the app groups the night's expenses in one place, with a live limit gauge — at the end you close or split.
steps: Tap to start an outing
Keep logging expenses through the night
At the end, close or split the bill

expense_map.q: How do I see my spends on the map?
expense_map.a: The "Spends on the map" screen shows where you spent on a satellite map. Spends at the same place are grouped; tap a point to see the list and total, and open any spend.
steps: Open "Spends on the map"
Tap a point or cluster to see the spends there
Tap a spend to open its detail

planner.q: What is the scenario planner for?
planner.a: It sets how much you can spend per category in the phase and lets you test scenarios (lean, balanced, relaxed) before deciding.
steps: Open the phase planner
Adjust limits per category or apply a preset
Compare the free-per-day of each scenario

planned.q: How do I reserve money for a planned purchase?
planned.a: List what you plan to buy (e.g. an 80 gift) and the app sets that amount aside from your free until you mark it as bought.
steps: Open planned purchases
Add the item and the estimated amount
When you buy it, mark it as done

simulator.q: How do I simulate an expense before making it?
simulator.a: In the simulator you type a hypothetical amount and see the effect on your free and projection — the classic "can I spend?".
steps: Open the simulator
Type the amount you're thinking of spending
See the impact before deciding

converter.q: How do I convert a price to my currency?
converter.a: The converter uses the rate the app already stored to show how much a price in another currency is in yours — e.g. 50 USD in reais.
steps: Open the currency converter
Type the amount and pick the currencies
See the result in your base currency

comparator.q: How do I know which pack is the better buy?
comparator.a: The cost-benefit comparator works out the real price per kg, litre or unit of each option and points to the cheapest — e.g. 120g for 1€ vs 200g for 2€. It works on a trip and in day-to-day life.
steps: Open the cost-benefit comparator
Enter each item's price, quantity and unit
See the price per unit and which one wins

funds.q: What are allowances and pots and how do I use them?
funds.a: Allowances split your budget per leg of the trip (e.g. Barcelona); pots set money apart for a goal (e.g. 150 for gifts) that doesn't count toward "how much I can spend today".
steps: Open allowances and pots
Create a allowance (a phase) or a pot (a goal)
Each expense draws from the chosen allowance or pot

piggy.q: What is the piggy bank and where do I see what I saved?
piggy.a: When you spend less than the day's free, the leftover becomes the piggy bank — savings you follow in the statement. E.g. 12 left over today.
steps: On the home screen, tap the piggy bank
See the total saved and the statement
Follow how much each day added

wallets.a: Each wallet (card, cash, account) has its own balance; when you log an expense you choose which wallet it came from.
steps: Open wallets
Create or edit a wallet and its balance
Pick the wallet when logging each expense

income.q: How do I record incoming money (income)?
income.a: Log entries like salary, reimbursement or deposit to follow what comes in, not only what goes out.
steps: Open record income
Enter the amount and the source
Save to add it to your available money

spaces.q: Can I have more than one trip at the same time?
spaces.a: Yes. In Spaces you keep several trips and the Day-to-day together and switch between them in one tap.
steps: Open Spaces
Create a new trip or the Day-to-day
Tap to switch between them whenever you want

viagem.q: How do I edit the trip's dates and phases?
viagem.a: In the trip hub you see and adjust any phase in one place, using the phase selector.
steps: Open the trip hub
Use the selector to choose the phase
Edit dates, budget or create another phase

profiles.a: They store the typical value of each expense type (e.g. bar, market) that the app uses to suggest and forecast better.
steps: Open activity profiles
Adjust the typical value of each category
Save so the AI uses it in suggestions

split.q: How do I split a bill with friends?
split.a: Photograph the bill (or type the items) and split by item, evenly or just your share — you can use the live table by passing the phone.
steps: Open split bill and add the receipt or items
Choose to split by item, evenly or just yours
Confirm who pays what and close

settle.q: How do I settle up and remind who owes me?
settle.a: Settle up opens with "Resolve now" (what to accept, remind or confirm first) and a single People list with a status badge — connected, invited or no app. You can remind, record a payment and confirm what you received; with a connected person, everything updates in real time.
steps: Open settle up
Clear what's under "Resolve now" first
See each person and their balance in the People list
Remind, record or confirm a received payment

reimbursement.q: I got the money back — how do I record the reimbursement?
reimbursement.a: When you receive a payment back, record the settlement and mark how it was made (Pix, Wise, cash…). The receiver confirms the payment, so the person's balance clears on both sides.
steps: In settle up, open the person who paid you
Tap record received reimbursement
Enter the amount and how it was paid, then confirm

group_split.q: How do I split many expenses with a group (Tricount-style)?
group_split.a: Create a group split and log every expense (manual, receipt photo or AI), with one or many payers and an equal or custom split. Right at creation you pick connected friends and trip people — they get an invite and the group only joins their app once they accept. Whoever marks "paid" stays neutral (never red) until the receiver confirms, and every move is kept in the history. You can also share a link for people without the app.
steps: In Split, open group splits and create one
Pick connected or trip people (or type the names) and log the expenses
Invite in the app or share the link — the person accepts to join
Track who paid and who's pending and confirm received payments

copilot.q: What does the Copilot show me?
copilot.a: It reads your data and sums up how the trip is doing and where it's heading, with practical saving tips.
steps: Open the Copilot
Read the current insights
Tap an insight to jump straight to the action

impact.q: How do I see the projection to the end of the trip?
impact.a: The impact screen details planned vs. spent and projects whether the money lasts to the end of the phase at the current pace.
steps: Open view impact
Compare planned and spent
See the projection and adjust the pace

rescue.q: I blew the budget — now what?
rescue.a: The rescue plan (SOS) builds a path back on track, suggesting where to cut without suffocating.
steps: Open the rescue (SOS)
See how much needs rebalancing
Follow the suggested cuts plan

backup.q: How do I back up and restore my data?
backup.a: You save a copy of the data (or export a spreadsheet) and can bring it from another device whenever you want — all in your control.
steps: Open backup and import
Tap export to save a copy
To restore, import the saved file

import_wise.q: How do I import my expenses from Wise?
import_wise.a: Bring the Wise statement via CSV and classify everything at once, without retyping each expense.
steps: Open import from Wise
Select the statement CSV file
Review the categories and confirm the import

privacy_location.q: How do location and the privacy of my data work?
privacy_location.a: Your data stays on the device. Location is only read with the system's permission and you turn it off whenever you want in settings.
steps: Open settings
Find the location option
Turn off place tagging if you prefer

customize_home.q: How do I customize the home screen?
customize_home.a: You choose which cards appear on the home screen and in what order, keeping what matters most to you at hand.
steps: Open customize home
Toggle the cards you want on or off
Drag to reorder and save

notifications.q: How do I turn notifications on or mute them?
notifications.a: Warnings, backup reminders and pace alerts live in one place. When a connected friend charges you, pays you or invites you to a group, the alert arrives instantly — also in the notification center and as a pending action on the home screen.
steps: Open notifications
See the pending actions (charges, payments, invites)
Choose which alerts you want and mute the rest

about.q: How do I update the app and see what's new?
about.a: The About screen shows the current version, what's new in each update and how to fetch the newest version.
steps: Open About the app
See the version and what's new
Reload to fetch the newest version

settings.q: Where do I change mode, theme, currency and language?
settings.a: In settings you adjust mode, theme, currency, language, alerts and everything else about the app.
steps: Open settings
Pick the preference (theme, currency, language…)
The app applies the change right away

simple_mode.q: What is simple mode and how does it change the app?
simple_mode.a: Simple mode keeps only the essentials at hand — Home, Expenses, Trip and Settings in the bottom bar — and tucks advanced features away. Nothing is deleted: search and links still reach everything. Complete mode reopens the Copilot and the rest.
steps: Open Settings under Preferences
Pick Simple or Complete mode
Switch anytime — nothing is lost, it just moves

funds.what_body: These are your budget buckets. A SEGMENT is a leg of the trip (e.g. Barcelona, €600); a POT is money set apart for a goal (e.g. Gifts, €100). Every logged expense draws from one of them.
funds.pool_card_body: The green value is what's STILL LEFT. The line below shows usage: "€350 / €2,000" = you've spent €350. Tap the card to open editing, reserves and envelopes.
funds.scope_body: A allowance applies to one or more phases (e.g. "Barcelona + Lisbon"); a pot applies to the whole trip. Linking the right phases makes "how much can I spend today" more honest.
funds.future_floors_body: Money you want to KEEP for a phase still ahead — it disappears from today's available amount. Example: €300 reserved for Lisbon stops being counted while you're in Barcelona.
funds.envelopes_body: Partitions inside the allowance or pot. Example: a €100 "Gifts" envelope locks that money — it leaves your free margin but stays there until you decide to use it.
funds.add_body: Tap here, choose whether it's a allowance (a phase) or a pot (a goal), and enter a name and amount. Example: a "Gifts" pot with €100.

planner.what_body: Here you build the phase plan: what you intend to do and how many times. The app multiplies each category by its typical value and shows whether it fits the budget.
planner.free_margin_body: How much of the phase budget is NOT committed yet. Example: €700 budget and a €530 plan → €170 free. If it goes negative (red), you planned more than you have.
planner.categories_body: Each card is a category (Dinner out, Bar, Museums...) with the typical value the app learned from your real expenses. Example: typical dinner €20.
planner.quantities_body: The − and + buttons change how many times you plan to do that in the phase. Example: 4× €20 dinners = €80 of the budget committed to dinners.
planner.recommendation_body: When the plan exceeds the budget, the app suggests where to cut so the math closes — you decide whether to apply it or adjust manually.

planned.what_body: They're buys you ALREADY KNOW you'll make but haven't yet. Example: €150 of skincare creams and €200 of clothes. Instead of just keeping it in your head, you log it here and the app accounts for it.
planned.reserve_body: With the reserve on, the estimated amount leaves your "free to spend" right now. Example: you plan €150 of creams → your free drops €150 today, so you don't spend that money by accident.
planned.tracking_body: Not sure yet? Turn the reserve off: the purchase stays on the list as a reminder but does NOT touch what's available. Example: "maybe €90 sneakers" you'll decide on later.
planned.bought_body: Tap "I bought it" and the app creates the real expense and closes the plan — the reserve becomes a real cost, never counted twice. Example: reserved €150, bought for €130 → €130 logged and the reserve disappears.
planned.multi_store_body: Buying the creams in different places? In "I bought it", turn off "mark as bought" and log each part. Example: €40 at the pharmacy, €50 at Primor, €60 at Druni — the reserve shrinks with each one.

wallets.what_body: A wallet is WHERE the money physically is: cash, card, account. Example: "Pocket" (cash) and "Wise card". It's different from a allowance/pot, which is the budget.
wallets.balance_body: The balance is derived from logged expenses: you started with €100 cash and logged a €13 market run paid in cash → the app shows €87.
wallets.default_body: When an expense doesn't say where it came from, it lands in the default wallet. Make your everyday one the default.
wallets.reconcile_body: Count your real cash and type what you have. Example: the app expected €87 and you counted €80 → it creates a €7 adjustment so reality matches.
wallets.vs_funds_body: Allowance/pot = budget (where money comes from in the plan). Wallet = physical place (where it is right now). A €20 dinner draws from the allowance/pot AND the "Card" wallet.

phase_edit.what_body: Phases are the chapters of your trip — e.g. "Barcelona" (10 days) and "Lisbon" (5 days). Each phase has its own dates, budget and activities.
phase_edit.dates_body: Changing dates recalculates the daily budget. Example: €700 over 10 days = €70/day; stretching to 14 days makes it €50/day.
phase_edit.activities_body: Enable only what makes sense in the phase. Example: "Beach" on in Barcelona, off in Madrid — the Planner and Outing only offer what's active.
phase_edit.events_body: Events are one-off expenses with reserved money. Example: "Coldplay concert" on Jul 12 with €60 reserved — the app guards that amount until the event day.

outing.what_body: The outing tracks your night in real time: every drink or bill goes in with one tap and the app shows where you stand against your limits.
outing.gauge_body: The dot is your current total over the 3 zones: green (up to target), orange (up to ceiling) and red (up to max). The pill value is only YOUR share of split items.
outing.limits_body: Target = what you'd like to spend (e.g. €15). Ceiling = still acceptable (€25). Max = stop here (€35). Crossing the target means taking money away from other plans.
outing.quick_add_body: One tap logs the value — +€3 for the beer, +€5 for the cocktail. The values belong to this session and can be edited via "adjust".
outing.items_body: Every logged expense shows up here. An undetailed item ("tap to detail") opens the "what was it?" question — answer later, no rush.
outing.end_body: Ending opens the review: confirm the total (you can correct it to match the tab), pick the wallet that paid and flag an atypical night — atypical nights don't teach the app.

backup.what_body: Your data lives ONLY on this device — there is no cloud. If the phone breaks or the browser wipes data, the backup is the only way back.
backup.export_body: Creates a file with EVERYTHING (expenses, phases, funds, settings) and opens the share sheet — send it to Drive, Files or your email. Example: send it to yourself every Friday during the trip.
backup.save_body: Writes the same file straight to the Downloads folder, without the share sheet. Example: save it before bed and copy it to your computer later.
backup.import_body: Restores from a backup you sent or saved earlier. Before applying, the app previews what changes: new, updated and conflicting records — and you choose merge or replace all.
backup.csv_body: A spreadsheet for Excel/Sheets — great for analyzing expenses, not for restoring. Advanced mode includes every technical column.
